title: Dossier catalog and new-dossier creation in ANDS Studio
walkthrough:
You land on a page with a top bar reading "ANDS Studio · dossier manager", followed by a user chip and navigation chips: "Help", "Portfolio", "Registry", "Correspondence", and "Guided journey →". Below, the heading "Your product dossiers" sits beside a "New dossier +" button. An explanatory paragraph states that a Dossier ID "is the permanent file for one product at Health Canada" and that your workspace's data is isolated from other clients.

If you have no dossiers, a notice says "No dossiers yet. Create one to start building a submission." (While the list fetches, you briefly see "Loading dossiers…".)

Clicking "New dossier +" (the button toggles to "Cancel") opens an inline card with two fields: "Dossier ID" (placeholder "e123456") and "Product name" (placeholder "Drugazole 10 mg tablet"). Small print explains: "Health Canada issues your Dossier ID when you file a Dossier ID Request through REP (via your CESG account)." — so you need to know the HC-issued ID format up front. If you don't have one, a link-style button offers "No ID yet? Start with a placeholder →", which auto-fills a generated ID starting with "d" (e.g. d482913). You then press "Create & open →" (it shows "Creating…" while busy). If your ID doesn't match the required pattern, a red notice appears: "Dossier ID must be one letter + 6–7 digits (e.g. e123456)".

On success you are taken straight into the dossier's Module 1 workspace: a left section tree, a central section panel, and a right rail showing a submission tower, a progress bar with "required sections complete" counts, and three readiness flags — "Documents", "Fee", "Valid eCTD".

Back on the catalog, each dossier appears as a clickable tile in a grid showing its ID, product title, submission type ("CS-BE"), a progress bar, and a status chip: either "Ready to file" or a count like "3/5 modules". Placeholder dossiers carry an extra chip, "draft ID — set real ✎"; clicking it opens a browser prompt: "Enter the Dossier ID issued by Health Canada (one letter + 6–7 digits, e.g. e123456). All documents, sequences and history move with it." Each tile also has a small "✕" delete button; clicking it triggers a native confirm dialog: "Delete dossier ⟨id⟩ and all of its documents? This cannot be undone." Renaming and deleting both rely on native browser prompt/confirm dialogs rather than in-app modals.
